def is_safe_name(name: str) -> bool:
    """True when `name` is a plain, single-component file name that stays inside `notes`."""
    ex is_safe_name("a.txt") == True
    ex is_safe_name("") == False
    ex is_safe_name("..") == False
    ex is_safe_name("../secret.txt") == False
    ex is_safe_name("sub/a.txt") == False
    ex is_safe_name("/etc/passwd") == False
    ex is_safe_name("a\\b") == False
    if name == "" or name == "." or name == "..":
        return False
    if "/" in name or "\\" in name:
        return False
    return True

def read_note(name: str) -> str uses fs:
    """Text of the file `name` inside the directory `notes`, or "" if it is missing or unreadable. Any name that would reach outside `notes` (such as "../x" or an absolute path) also gives ""."""
    if not is_safe_name(name):
        return ""
    text = ""
    with fs = fs.sub("notes"):
        text = fs.read_text(name) else ""
    return text
